lessons.title: What is statistics, really?
lessons.summary: From a small sample to a bigger question.
lessons.body: Statistics helps us learn from data while accounting for variation and uncertainty. Descriptive statistics summarize what we observed. Inferential statistics use a sample to learn about a wider population.
lessons.example: Imagine you ask 40 students how many hours they sleep. Their average describes those 40 students. Estimating the average for every student requires thinking about how the 40 were selected. A large convenience sample can still be biased.
lessons.takeaway: A sample is a window into a population. How that window was chosen matters.
lessons.bangla: নমুনা থেকে বড় জনগোষ্ঠী সম্পর্কে জানতে হলে নমুনা কীভাবে নেওয়া হয়েছে, সেটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।

lessons.title: Mean, median & the unusual value
lessons.summary: Three ways to understand a typical observation.
lessons.body: The mean adds all values and divides by their count. The median is the middle value after sorting. Both describe location, but they respond differently to unusual values.
lessons.example: For daily study times of 1, 2, 2, 3, and 12 hours, the mean is 4 hours and the median is 2. The 12-hour value pulls the mean upward. Neither summary is automatically wrong; choose based on the question and show the distribution.
lessons.takeaway: Look at the shape of the data before choosing a single summary.
lessons.bangla: অস্বাভাবিক বড় মান গড়কে টেনে বাড়াতে পারে। মধ্যক তুলনামূলক কম বদলায়।

lessons.title: A confidence interval is a method
lessons.body: A confidence interval gives a range calculated using a procedure with a specified long-run coverage rate, under its assumptions. A 95% procedure would cover the fixed population parameter in about 95% of repeated samples.
lessons.example: Suppose an estimated mean difference is 4 points with a 95% interval from 1 to 7. Report the estimated difference and the uncertainty together. In frequentist inference, we do not interpret this particular interval as having a 95% probability of containing the fixed parameter.
lessons.takeaway: Confidence intervals address sampling uncertainty; they do not automatically fix bias or confounding.
lessons.bangla: আস্থার ব্যবধান অনিশ্চয়তা বোঝায়; এটি পক্ষপাত বা ভুল গবেষণা নকশা দূর করে না।

lessons.title: What a p-value can tell you
lessons.summary: Evidence under a model, not a verdict.
lessons.body: A p-value is the probability, under the null model and its assumptions, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
lessons.example: A small p-value can signal incompatibility with the null model, but does not tell you that an effect is large, useful, or causal. A large p-value does not prove there is no effect. Examine effect estimates, intervals, design, and the full context.
lessons.takeaway: Ask how large the effect is and how uncertain the estimate is.
lessons.bangla: ছোট p-value মানেই বড় বা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রভাব নয়। প্রভাবের পরিমাণ ও অনিশ্চয়তাও দেখুন।

lessons.title: Regression: a line through the story
lessons.summary: Separate a fitted average from individual variation.
lessons.body: Simple linear regression models the conditional mean of an outcome as a linear function of a predictor. Ordinary least squares chooses the intercept and slope that minimize the sum of squared vertical residuals.
lessons.example: If a fitted equation is score = 50 + 4 × practice hours, the fitted mean score at 3 hours is 62. Individual scores can differ from 62. Prediction for a new individual generally has more uncertainty than estimating the mean at that predictor value.
lessons.takeaway: A fitted trend is an estimate, not the true population line and not a causal proof.
lessons.bangla: রেখাটি গড় সম্পর্কের অনুমান; প্রতিটি পর্যবেক্ষণ রেখার ওপর থাকবে না।

lessons.title: Association is not causation
lessons.summary: A relationship needs a careful explanation.
lessons.body: Two variables can move together because one affects the other, because a third factor affects both, or because of selection and other biases. Statistical adjustment only helps under suitable assumptions.
lessons.example: Students who practice more may score higher. Prior preparation and motivation can affect both practice and performance. A regression association alone cannot establish the effect of making a student practice one extra hour.
lessons.takeaway: Causal questions need a credible design and explicit assumptions.
lessons.bangla: দুটি বিষয়ের সম্পর্ক থাকলেই একটি অন্যটির কারণ—এমন বলা যায় না।
